title: The Concept of Other Minds
text:
In philosophy of mind, the problem of 'other minds' addresses how knowledge of mental states—such as beliefs or feelings—is gained concerning entities other than oneself. Since direct access to another person's conscious experience is impossible, understanding their internal life requires inference and assumption.

The assumption that all rational agents possess subjective experiences is foundational to interpersonal ethics and social theory. This gap between self-knowledge and the knowledge of others leads to philosophical debates regarding empathy, qualia, and the limits of objective description.
